worker_target_description: Experiment 1: preference for a favorite movie star kiss versus $50 cash in certainty versus 1% probability conditions; between-condition chi-square test of the probability-outcome interaction.
worker_notes: Only es_value_o was assigned. Other fields and the replication side are unassigned placeholders. The requested OR is not printed for Experiment 1; retain the printed chi-square test statistic 4.91 without conversion. The same test is printed with p < .05 and N = 40. No OR has been computed from the reported choice percentages. Matched by the Experiment 1 kisses-versus-cash outcome and certainty manipulation, not by numeric correspondence. PDF p. 187 was rendered and visually checked against canonical text; canonical OCR uses ␹2, ⫽, and ⬍ for the corresponding printed mathematical symbols.

coding_context.description: Whether to prefer an affectively attractive option (a kiss from a favorite movie star) or a financially attractive option ($50) depends on certainty
coding_context.reported_success_quote:
The difference was significant, p =
.002, odds ratio (OR) = 0.87, d = −0.08, 95% CI = [−0.13,
−0.03], but in the direction opposite the prediction of
the hypothesis (i.e., that affectively attractive choices
are more preferred when they are uncertain rather than
definite). The overall effect was much smaller than in
the original study and in the opposite direction (d =
−0.08, 95% CI = [−0.13, −0.03], vs. original d = 0.74).
